title: Polyatomic Posse: Polyatomic Ions — ItsDrDan
author: Dr. Dan (ItsDrDan)

chapters.CHEM 3A: Chapter 4: naming ions and compounds (Green Sheet polyatomic ions)
chapters.CHEM 1A: Chapter 2: chemical nomenclature (Green Sheet polyatomic ions)

description: Polyatomic ion practice built on the Green Sheet, for CHEM 3A and CHEM 1A (default 1A; add ?course=3A). Every one of the 30 Green Sheet ions (oxyanion table, other common ions, naming-rule examples and sulfite from the solubility table, including both acetate formulas). Four games: Write the Formula, Name the Ion, Ion Families (given chlorate, build perchlorate, chlorite and hypochlorite; given sulfate, find sulfite; carbonate to hydrogen carbonate; phosphate to hydrogen and dihydrogen phosphate), and Charge Check (tap just the charge), plus Skill Check Prep: 10 mixed questions, then a study plan with the missed ions and mistake types. Smart typing turns SO4^2-, SO42- or SO4-2 into SO₄²⁻, and the formula and the charge are graded separately. Mistake catchers name the slip: -ite/-ate swap, per-/hypo- mix-up, charge sign, charge size, missing subscript, ammonium is positive, and the hydrogen- prefix (one less negative). Decks don't repeat an ion until the set is done. Hints, step-by-step help, Professor Tips, a Green Sheet ion list, a periodic table, XP, ranks and 10 achievements. New: Ion Builder lab questions inside Ion Families: predict the charge, tap +O / −O / +H⁺ / −H⁺ to build the ion and watch the charge, explain why, then write the same change in another family. Oxyanion Table mode: fill in the -ate table laid out like the periodic table (groups 13–17, periods 2–5) and colored by the T43 method (blue T: B, C, N, Si = 3 O; purple 4: P, S, As, Se, Te = 4 O; pink 3: Cl, Br, I = 3 O), by typing each cell’s ion or, as an easier warm-up, placing “□O₄²⁻”-style tiles where the O count and charge fit. A “Learn with Dr. Dan” video player at the bottom (and a Video button by Hint) shows from the ItsDrDan YouTube channel (T43 method, Green Sheet walkthrough, Writing Ionic Formulas Part II), cued to the relevant spot.
